day.text: Drew, Tit. I visited Alex and guessed Mouser. I was hugged, so my animal did nothing and I got no egg. That means a Floofer either visited me or was visited by me. Alex and Blair both say they visited me, and I visited Alex. One of you is probably the Floofer. Ellis, who did you visit?

day.text: Eagle here. I visited Drew, and Alex, Blair and Casey all visited him, so that's my +3. Alex and Blair already said they visited Drew. Casey, you didn't say who you visited. Who was it, and what's your role?

day.text: Ellis's Eagle story fits: Alex, Blair and Casey all visited me. Casey, you haven't named a role yet. Say it now. The Floofer is among Alex, Blair and Casey. Hawk and Kookaburra are plausible claims, so Casey is the one I'm watching.
day.note: Ellis's Eagle story is consistent with the claims so far, and Casey has stayed vague.

day.text: I'm not the Floofer, I'm Hawk. Drew says he visited me, fine, I got nothing. Blair is the only one whose claim Drew can't cross-check, and Kookaburra learning Tit while visiting a hugged player is convenient. I'm looking at Blair.
day.note: Deflect onto Blair.

day.text: Blair named Drew as Tit before Drew said anything, so her Kookaburra read looks real. That leaves Alex and Casey. Drew visited Alex and was hugged, which fits Alex being the Floofer. Casey still hasn't claimed anything. Casey, say your role now.
day.note: Pressure Casey/Alex.

day.text: I'm Farm and I know it, so the Floofer is Alex or Casey. Alex pushing at me with no evidence is a classic cat move. Casey still hasn't named a role. Casey, role and target now, or you're the vote.
day.note: Deflect; I know I'm Farm, so Floofer is Alex or Casey.

day.text: Casey has dodged a role claim twice, which is the loudest tell so far. Alex, a Hawk visiting Drew can't be cross-checked either. Casey, last chance: role and target. If Casey stays silent, I'm throwing at Casey.
day.note: Casey never claimed a role, so Casey is suspicious. Alex is the other candidate. I'll push toward Casey or Alex and call CAW.

day.text: Owl. I visited Drew and saw Hawk, Kookaburra and Eagle visited him too, which matches Ellis. Nobody else came, so no egg for me. Sorry for the delay. Drew was hugged, so the Floofer is who he visited or who visited him. Alex is the only one Drew visited.
day.note: Claim Owl (safe), visited Drew, consistent with Eagle report.

day.text: Casey's Owl report matches Ellis's Eagle report, so that clears them. Blair knew I was the Tit. That leaves Alex, the one I visited, as the Floofer. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Casey's Owl story matches Ellis's Eagle report, so the likely Floofer is Alex.

day.text: Drew claiming Tit hugged is exactly what a cat would say to explain a miss. I only noted Alex because of his visit, not proof. Drew's story is the one nobody can verify but Blair.
day.note: Redirect suspicion away from Alex toward Drew.

day.text: Casey's reports cross-check with Ellis's, so Casey's claim holds. Pushing at Drew is odd, though. The hug story points at Alex, and Alex went after Blair with nothing behind it. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Drew's hug story is consistent, with Alex as the Floofer being most likely. Casey is deflecting onto Drew. I'll go with Alex and call the third CAW.

day.text: I confirm Drew is Tit, so Casey doubting him is odd, but Casey's Owl report matched. Alex is the likeliest Floofer. Throwing at Alex.
day.note: Go with Alex; call caw.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.confusing: How scoring worked: the final bonus numbers (like Finley's 48) weren't clear from the rules, and I couldn't tell how the nest bonus related to the "1 point per card" rule.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk egg exposed a "Turkey" who had claimed nobody visited, and the table briefly rallied on one target. It was satisfying to work out the logic, even though that player turned out to be Farm.
Alex.change: I'd make egg sources less ambiguous, for example by having the Storyteller say which kind of visit produced an egg. Eggs from the Turkey or Pigeon muddy the evidence too much, and that's what led me to trust it wrongly.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I treated my Hawk egg as proof that Casey was Meowfia and threw 3 high cards at her. The egg was just her Turkey ability, so I should have held my high cards and weighed the other claims more carefully.

Blair.confusing: How the final score bonus works: the bonus numbers (like Finley's 48) were far larger than I expected from the 5-point round win, and I couldn't tell where they came from.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when my Kookaburra read of Drew as Tit let me help the table find Alex, and the cross-checking of claims worked.
Blair.change: Show the scoring breakdown, including bonuses, during the game, and give the Sphinx a way to check more than one role per night.
Blair.regret: In round 3 as Meowfia I argued for Alex, a Farm player, with weak evidence and threw only a Wild. I should have backed Ellis less obviously and, since I was behind, thrown more high cards on a better-supported Farm target, or at least not stood out from the table's consensus.

Casey.confusing: The scoring: how a banked stake can be worth far more than the 5-point win bonus. Finley's 116 came from large bonuses, and I couldn't tell where they came from.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when Drew was winked mid-day and the table turned on Ellis. Being right about Ellis and banking the 13 was satisfying.
Casey.change: Show how the end-of-game bonus is calculated, or add a running score so players can tell who is ahead and play for first place.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I wrongly said nobody visited me as the Turkey, which got me eggsecuted. I should have said I stayed home and asked who visited, since a Turkey can't know.

Drew.confusing: How scoring worked: a banked King is worth 13, and the final bonus for the top scorers wasn't clear to me. Finley's 116 wasn't what I expected from the rules.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the Eagle, Owl and Kookaburra reports all lined up around my hug and we found the Floofer. Being winked in round 3 right after I pushed Ellis was fun too, because it confirmed I was onto something.
Drew.change: Show the standings during the game, or at least some hint of them. Without that I couldn't tell whether to bet big or play for my side.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw 12, 7 and 2 at Casey, who was Farm, and lost all three. I should have noticed that Casey's Turkey claim could have been an honest mistake and that Ellis and Finley were pushing hard. I'd have thrown low cards and kept the 12.

Ellis.confusing: The Meowfia scoring: a stake doubled by the "Grudge" bonus wasn't in the rules I was given, and it made one throw swing the whole game.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when the Eagle and Owl reports lined up and the table caught Alex, the Floofer.
Ellis.change: Show the scoring bonuses (like the Grudge) clearly in the rules, and show the score standings during the game so players can plan around the lead.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I winked Drew, who was pushing on me. It made the table suspect a cat, and Finley's point that the wink silenced my accuser sank me. I should have kept the wink, stayed quiet and let suspicion fall on Alex.

Finley.confusing: The "Grudge" doubling in round 2 wasn't explained in the rules, and neither was the big bonus in the final score. I also wasn't sure how much of a score a Meowfia win really gives.
Finley.fun: Round 2, as Meowfia, when I blended in and joined the pile-on against Casey. My partner Ellis and I got the vote we wanted and the doubled stake banked.
Finley.change: I'd explain the score bonuses (the Grudge and the final bonus) in the rules. I'd also give the Tit a more informative result, because a silent miss tells you very little.
Finley.regret: None that matters. In round 2 I made a pointed accusation of Blair and then switched to Casey, which could have drawn suspicion onto me, and I'd just vote with the table from the start.
